rules: I am · He / she / it is · You / we / they are
Choose am, is or are to match the person or people in the sentence.
I am happy. She is a teacher.
I / you / we / they have · He / she / it has
Have and has tell us what someone owns.
We have books. He has a bag.
He = a boy · She = a girl · They = two or more people
Use his for something a boy owns. Use her for something a girl owns.
Ali is kind. He is kind. It is her book.
I play · She plays · They play
Use it for routines. Many verbs take s or es after he, she or it.
She walks to school every day.
Use it for actions happening now.
play → played · go → went · eat → ate
Use it for actions in the past. Many verbs take ed. Some verbs have a special past form.
will + verb · am / is / are going to + verb
Use it for the future. After will or going to, use the base form of the verb.
She will visit grandma. We are going to play.
Inside · on top · below · at the back · in the middle of two things.
The cat is under the table.
Use taller to compare two things. The tallest is higher than all the other things.
Tower B is taller. Tower C is the tallest.

Retained as supported revision for a lower to lower-middle ability Year 6 class: sections 9–10 permit teachers to revisit Years 1–5 grammar, and Appendix 1 confirms the upper-primary foundations. This pack is prerequisite practice, not complete coverage of new Year 6 grammar or full learning standards. Original mission IDs, task order, prompts, answers, options and object definitions are unchanged so existing pupil progress remains valid. The five comparison tasks only gained missing full-sentence feedback. Game scores are not PBD performance levels.
